active_family: 647 candidate: direct sequence-level mixed-coordinate path flow
current_bottleneck: The one-step/free-running transition family is capped: it learns local daily moves, support validity, and co-movement, but it repeatedly fails full-path conditional probability allocation. Auxiliary losses and sampling calibration move one metric group while damaging another.
last_result_summary: 646a closed the post-645 decision. 641a remains the clean native joint baseline, but 643a and 645a show that sampling knobs and local finetune objectives are not enough. The repeated mechanism is that one-step AR training is misaligned with the evaluated object: a 30-day conditional future path distribution.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 647a as a minimal direct sequence-level mixed-coordinate flow: condition on history level/increment scores, generate the entire future [horizon, channels] tensor jointly in 641a's mixed coordinate, use one shared temporal/channel transformer denoiser, and evaluate IV 11-suite plus joint-panel audit. No separate IV/factor treatment, no retrieval, no low-rank decoder, no stress deck.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 612a is the highest IV-count native joint run at 6/11 but has a degenerate source-scale mechanism and poor anchor-factor joint audit. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 641a is the clean native joint baseline because it removes post-hoc gluing and recovers strong anchor-factor realism, but it is still only 4/11 on the IV suite.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
